description: Nutrition and dietary recommendations for menopause

entries.title: Calcium for Bone Health
entries.content: Calcium is crucial for maintaining bone density and preventing osteoporosis after menopause. Women need 1200mg of calcium daily after menopause. Getting calcium from food sources is ideal, but supplements can help if dietary intake is insufficient.
food_sources: Leafy greens: Kale, collard greens, bok choy
Fortified foods: Orange juice, cereals, plant milks
Fish with bones: Sardines, canned salmon
entries.supplements: Consider if dietary intake insufficient; take with vitamin D for absorption
tips: Spread calcium intake throughout day for better absorption
Don't take more than 500mg at once

entries.title: Vitamin D for Bone and Overall Health
entries.description: Essential vitamin for calcium absorption and bone health
entries.content: Vitamin D is essential for calcium absorption and bone health. It also supports immune function and mood. Many people are deficient, especially those with limited sun exposure. Vitamin D is crucial for preventing osteoporosis after menopause.
entries.recommended_intake: 800-1000 IU per day; some may need more
food_sources: Fortified foods: Milk, orange juice, cereals
entries.sunlight: 10-30 minutes of midday sun several times per week (varies by skin tone and location)
entries.supplements: Often necessary, especially in winter or with limited sun exposure
entries.testing: Blood test can check vitamin D levels if deficiency suspected

entries.title: B Vitamins for Energy and Mood
entries.description: B vitamins support energy, mood, and cognitive function
entries.content: B vitamins, especially B6 and B12, are important during menopause. B6 helps with mood regulation, energy, and reducing irritability by supporting serotonin and dopamine production. B12 aids nerve function, energy, and cognitive health, helping combat brain fog.
key_b_vitamins: B12: Nerve function, energy, cognitive health, combats brain fog
food_sources: B6: Poultry, fish, potatoes, chickpeas, bananas
B12: Meat, fish, eggs, dairy, fortified cereals (B12 is only in animal products)
Folate: Leafy greens, legumes, fortified grains
entries.supplements: B-complex supplement may help; B12 especially important for vegetarians/vegans

entries.title: Omega-3 Fatty Acids
entries.description: Healthy fats for heart and brain health
entries.content: Omega-3 fatty acids support heart health, reduce inflammation, and may help stabilize mood during menopause. They're important for cardiovascular health, which becomes a greater concern after menopause.
food_sources: Fatty fish: Salmon, mackerel, sardines, herring (2-3 servings per week)
entries.supplements: Fish oil or algae-based omega-3 supplements if not eating fish regularly

entries.title: Balanced Diet for Overall Health
entries.content: A balanced, nutrient-rich diet is foundational for managing menopause symptoms and maintaining health. Focus on whole foods, fruits, vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, and healthy fats while limiting processed foods, sugar, and saturated fats.
principles: Eat variety of fruits and vegetables (aim for colorful plate)
Choose whole grains over refined grains
Include lean proteins (fish, poultry, legumes, tofu)
Healthy fats (olive oil, nuts, avocado, fatty fish)
Limit processed foods, added sugars, and saturated fats

entries.title: Foods to Limit or Avoid
entries.description: Foods that may worsen menopause symptoms
entries.content: Certain foods and beverages can trigger or worsen menopause symptoms, particularly hot flashes. Identifying and limiting your personal triggers can help manage symptoms.
common_triggers: Caffeine (coffee, tea, energy drinks) - can trigger hot flashes and worsen sleep
Alcohol - triggers hot flashes, disrupts sleep, affects mood
Spicy foods - can trigger hot flashes
Hot beverages - can trigger hot flashes
Sugary foods and drinks - blood sugar spikes, weight gain
High sodium foods - bloating, blood pressure
entries.approach: Keep a food diary to identify your personal triggers; everyone is different

entries.title: Phytoestrogen Foods
entries.description: Plant foods containing weak estrogen-like compounds
entries.content: Phytoestrogens are plant compounds with weak estrogen-like effects. Including phytoestrogen-rich foods in your diet may provide mild symptom relief for some women, though evidence is limited. They're part of a healthy diet regardless.
food_sources: Soybeans, tofu, tempeh, edamame, soy milk
entries.effectiveness: Limited and inconsistent evidence; effects much weaker than HRT
entries.safety: Food sources are safe; discuss supplements with doctor if history of breast cancer

entries.title: Beneficial Drinks and Beverages
entries.description: Hydrating and supportive beverages for menopause
entries.content: Certain beverages can help support hydration and provide beneficial nutrients during menopause. Staying well-hydrated is essential, especially with hot flashes and night sweats causing fluid loss.
recommended_drinks: Water: Best choice for hydration, especially important with hot flashes
Herbal teas: Spearmint, red clover, chasteberry may help balance hormones (limited evidence)
Green tea: Provides antioxidants and mild caffeine for energy
Coconut water: Replenishes electrolytes lost during hot flashes
Fortified plant milks: Provide calcium and vitamin D
entries.hydration_importance: Hot flashes and night sweats increase fluid loss; aim for 8+ glasses of water daily
beverages_to_limit: Caffeine: Can trigger hot flashes and disrupt sleep
Alcohol: Triggers hot flashes, disrupts sleep, affects mood
Sugary drinks: Blood sugar spikes, weight gain, inflammation
tips: Keep water bottle handy throughout day
Drink cool or room temperature beverages to avoid triggering hot flashes
Limit caffeine to morning hours only

entries.title: Magnesium for Sleep and Symptoms
entries.description: Essential mineral for sleep, mood, and hot flash relief
entries.content: Magnesium is an important mineral during menopause that supports sleep quality, reduces hot flashes, improves mood, and supports bone health. Many women are deficient in magnesium. It works synergistically with calcium and vitamin D for bone health and can help ease multiple menopausal symptoms.
benefits: Improves sleep quality and reduces insomnia
May reduce hot flash frequency and severity
Helps with muscle relaxation and reduces cramps
Supports bone health (works with calcium and vitamin D)
entries.recommended_intake: 320mg per day for women over 30; some may benefit from higher doses for sleep
food_sources: Leafy greens: Spinach, Swiss chard, kale
Nuts and seeds: Almonds, cashews, pumpkin seeds
Whole grains: Brown rice, quinoa, oats
entries.supplements: Magnesium glycinate is well-absorbed and gentle on stomach; often taken before bed for sleep support
entries.dosage_notes: Start with lower dose and increase gradually; too much can cause digestive upset
